intelligence.title: The Laws Settle the Day

intelligence.human_view: Sixteen hours of 429s, and the fix was his hand on the dashboard: five dollars a month, one purchase, and the wall is gone — and the verification was ours, a live write landed, a live read-back matched, a live delete cleaned up, on the same store that refused writes all morning (SN-2951). The fastest shape we have is a tap: he tapped the options widget at 15:44Z and Naya Notes' place closed in the same minute — under the tabs, not its own tab — and two minutes later the Feed Law moved the chip from the topic side to the type side, because "Naya Notes" is a kind of thing on the feed, not a topic (SN-2952, SN-2953). At 16:01Z he named the mode that governs everything after it: "the fast action plan" — he says something, it gets done right away and comes back right away; the visual agreement had sat 10 hours and the sidebar round took hours, not because the making was slow, but because each verified step waited for the next queue (SN-2954). In the same message he set the deadline — Personal complete today, all the way through — and gave the end slide its plus button and its two honest links (SN-2955, SN-2956, SN-2957). Then, from the end-buttons discussion, two laws in one pass: always a way back, and never a show-all on the visual — and the proof case arrived half an hour later, when he clicked into the collective agreement and couldn't go back (SN-2958, SN-2959). And over the staged Personal page he asked for the anatomy itself: "let's write the anatomy of a smart app" — what it has, how it functions, what will be where, and why (SN-2960).
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine a little box that can only hold 1,000 tiny notes a day — and every day it filled up and said "NO MORE!" Then Shawn bought a magic upgrade, and now the box can hold a MILLION notes a month! The box didn't move, the key didn't change — it just got bigger, all by itself! And imagine your feed is a special box that holds exactly THREE kinds of treasures: Naya's notes, smart notes, and posts! Nothing else fits in the box! And every room in your house has a door back to the hallway, so you never get stuck! And your favourite picture book goes one page at a time — each page a surprise — never all the pages glued together! And when you finish building with blocks, you show your friend RIGHT AWAY — no waiting on the shelf!
intelligence.grandma_view: It's like this, love — we had a little post box that only took a thousand letters a day, and Shawn went and bought the bigger box himself — five dollars a month — and now it takes a million letters. Same box, same key, just bigger. Your feed is a tidy little shelf that holds exactly three things: Naya's notes, smart notes, and posts — nothing else goes on that shelf. Every page has a little way back, like a door you came in through, so you never get stuck. The picture show goes one picture at a time, like turning the pages of a lovely book — but the letter you can read whole, that's perfectly fine. And before, we set every finished piece aside and waited hours before showing it — like a cake left cooling when everyone's hungry. Now we show it in that very same moment.
intelligence.naya_view: The laws settle the day: a feed is three things, nothing else; a project is a world you add; one filter row, kinds first, then topics. A back button on every page, elegant and blocking nothing. The visual is one slide at a time, always. Fast action: build a piece, verify it right away, show it the same pass — nothing sits, nothing held, nothing bundled. The page is a smart app, and the anatomy is its map.
